text:
sara: Heads-up: we're starting a staged rollout of the new rate-limit policy v2 for a subset of accounts (5% -> 20%). watching for 429s + auth regressions. pls read below and chime in.
raj: Can you drop the canary cohorts? Which customers are in the 5% and what time window?
sara: cohort: internal beta + 3 low-traffic customers (acme-dev, beta-shop, metrics-lab). start 10:30 PDT, step to 20% at 1h if signals look ok.
mike: Signals to monitor: 429 rate (global + per-customer), 95p latency for generation endpoints, auth error rate, and token-cost delta in billing dimension. If any signal spikes > 3x baseline for 10m, prepare to rollback.
lina: For rollback runbook: ping eng-platform, mark canary paused in console, revert policy via infra CLI, and notify customers + sales. Keep communication snippet ready.
sara: Repro steps to validate behavior locally for support: 1) curl with a customer key 2) hammer with burst pattern 3) check response headers for limit info. Example:```bash
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer pk_test_cust123" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
# look for: HTTP/1.1 429, X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining
```
raj: We recently had a case where burst allowances caused unexpected bill jumps — can we confirm the new policy doesn't expand burst windows for committed customers?
mike: Confirmed: v2 tightens burst-window default for hosted customers. dedicated/reserved keep prior semantics unless explicitly opted in. billing team okayed that to avoid surprises.
sara: deploy-bot: starting canary: rate-policy-v2 -> 5% traffic (ids: c-1001, c-2022, c-3033)
deploy-bot: canary started at 2026-03-17T10:30:00Z — monitoring hooks enabled (429,latency,auth,cost).
oncall-bot: ALERT: acme-dev observed 3x 429s in 5m window at 10:42 PDT. auto-throttle engaged.
lina: I'm looking at logs now — requests show header `x-rategroup: v2-strict` then immediate 429s for long streaming calls. probable mismatch with streaming batch thresholds.
mike: Action: pause canary (manual rollback) if 429s persist > 15m or customer tickets open. I'll prepare rollback command.
sara: rollback command (eng ops): ```bash
infractl policy rollback --name rate-policy-v2 --to-tag v1 --scope canary
```
raj: If we rollback, support, please issue this templated note to affected customers: "We're pausing a rate policy experiment impacting your account, service is restored to previous behavior while we investigate" — add incident link.
sara: Agreed. I'm assembling the customer messages and will post in #customer-success once rollback is live. :thumbsup:
mike: After rollback, we'll run a smaller config test focusing on streaming KV cache thresholds and re-run canary for a single customer.
lina: Also flag to docs to add a short note on burst allowances and how they show up on the Console token-cost dashboard.
sara: Thanks all — I'll update this thread when rollback completes or if metrics stabilize.
deploy-bot: canary paused at 2026-03-17T10:55:30Z per request by mike.
